name: New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA)
notes: Researched from NYCHA's public Pay Rent page on nyc.gov. Online one-time payments need the 9-digit Tenant ID and 9-digit Account Number (no login) by E-Check (free), Visa/MasterCard debit (0.8%) or credit incl. Amex/Discover (2.25%; fees go to a third-party vendor) - engine models the 2.25% credit rate. E-Bill is the free recurring electronic bill paid by E-Check with multiple payment sources. Phone Payment System 833-894-0899 (before 5 PM EST same-day credit). Mail: NYCHA, P.O. Box 5543, Binghamton, NY 13902-5543. Payroll deduction for City employees via the Self-Service Portal. Payment plans only in person at the property management office (photo ID, no down payment, max 40% of household income). Customer Contact Center 718-707-7771. The Self-Service Portal (Siebel) sign-in labels were not observed; identifier left as family default. No move-out notice process on this page (template notice kept, inferred). REVIEW 2026-10-09 (independent reviewer): verified the Pay Rent page (fees, E-Bill with split payment sources, phone cutoff, P.O. box, payroll deduction, in-person payment plans, REES 718-289-8100, contact center 718-707-7771). guestLookupFields can only express the Account Number; the real form also asks for the 9-digit Tenant ID (no schema field for it). No other changes.

help.title: Ways to pay NYCHA rent
paragraphs: Rent is due on the first of each month. Pay online or at the Self-Service Kiosk in your management office with your 9-digit Tenant ID and 9-digit Account Number, an email, a phone number and either bank details (E-Check) or a card.
E-Check is free. Visa or MasterCard debit cards cost 0.8% of the payment and Visa, MasterCard, American Express or Discover credit cards cost 2.25%; these fees go to a third-party vendor, not NYCHA.

You can also add NYCHA as a payee in your bank's bill pay, pay by phone at 833-894-0899, mail a check or money order, use payroll deduction if you are a City employee, or pay in person for a fee at an authorized credit union. Questions: Customer Contact Center 718-707-7771.

help.title: Paying by mail
paragraphs: Make the check or money order payable to New York City Housing Authority, write your account number on it and include the remittance slip. Mail it to NYCHA, P.O. Box 5543, Binghamton, NY 13902-5543. Mail early: delivery and processing take three to five business days. Never send cash.

help.title: E-Bill
paragraphs: E-Bill is free: you receive your rent bill electronically and pay by E-Check. You can store several payment sources and split a payment among them.

help.title: Paying by phone
paragraphs: Call the Phone Payment System at 833-894-0899. Payments made before 5 PM EST are credited the same day; later payments, and those on weekends or federal holidays, are credited the next business day. Allow three to five business days for your bank to show the payment.

help.title: Rent hardship and payment plans
paragraphs: To set up a payment plan, visit your property management office with photo ID. No down payment is required, monthly payments will not exceed 40% of household income, and the plan can be adjusted if your income changes. If your income dropped, submit an interim recertification through the Self-Service Portal.

The City's HRA One-Shot Deal can help with arrears (apply through ACCESS NYC or call 311 and ask for the Tenant Helpline), and Homebase offers emergency rental help through 311. Financial counseling is available through REES at 718-289-8100.

help.title: Payroll deduction
paragraphs: NYCHA and other City employees can sign up for payroll deduction in the Self-Service Portal. Half the monthly rent comes out of each of the first two paychecks of the month. To stop it, submit a termination form to your property management office.
